_note: Planning doc — organization detail. NOT a live entity. Reframes/expands the existing 'ninth_thesis' and 'secret_society' faction entities in data/factions.json. See ../campaign_arc.json for the big picture.
name: The Ninth Thesis

leader.identity: Dr. Ellery Voss (existing NPC — founder-descendant, already tagged independent/secretive)

purpose: Exists to uncover hidden evils in the world. Presently actively investigating the source of the escalating incidents at the Academy.

name_origin.description: Named for the Academy's first graduating class, hundreds of years ago, which had nine members. Each of the nine was required to write a thesis about their time at the Academy and how they intended to fit into the world upon graduating.
name_origin.the_missing_thesis: One of the nine original theses went missing. The organization found it years ago (predating the current incident investigation) and adopted it as the basis for its existence.

author.name: Wren Halloway
author.status: CONFIRMED (2026-08-02) — one of the nine members of the Academy's first graduating class. Name and backstory locked in as canon; already live in content/sessions/session_1.html, where Voss names her directly if the party asks who she's quoting.
author.background: Not a star student — quiet, watchful, kept to herself more than her eight classmates. Where the others wrote their mandatory graduation theses as the expected declarations of glory (dragons to fight, kingdoms to serve), Halloway spent her four years noticing things: whispered conversations that stopped when she entered a room, professors who locked their doors twice, classmates who weren't who their letters of introduction said they were. Her thesis broke from the form entirely — instead of stating her intentions for the world, she wrote what she'd actually learned at the Academy. That break from convention is very likely why it was the one thesis quietly pulled from the record rather than filed with the other eight.
author.afterward: What became of her after graduation is unrecorded — open/placeholder, not yet needed for the plot unless you want to use her later.

founding_document.excerpt: We were asked to write of what we intend to become, and so all around me my classmates wrote of glory. I found I could not join them. In four years here I learned exactly one lesson worth keeping, and it is this: no one is without a secret, and no one is without a reason for it. Not the students who whispered in the dueling yard past curfew. Not the professors who locked their doors twice. Not, I think, the three who built this place and told us it was built for one purpose, when I have walked its halls long enough to feel it was built for another. I do not say this as an accusation. I say it because a secret, once it is understood for what it is, is a kind of power — and I intend to spend the rest of my life learning to recognize it, wherever it is kept.
founding_document.excerpt_status: Draft — yours to revise or approve as-is.
founding_document.assessment: On its own the thesis is a little too subtle/abstract to prove anything. Combined with other data points the organization has gathered since, it forms a convincing argument that there's a secret source of evil somewhere on campus.
founding_document.veil_knowledge_boundary: Halloway did not know about the veil specifically — she sensed only that the founders had an unstated deeper purpose. This matters for continuity: campaign_arc.json states the founders never passed along their veil knowledge to anyone. Aldric Voss founding the organization around her instinct (see below) doesn't contradict that — he gave the Ninth Thesis a mandate to watch for hidden danger, not the specific secret of the veil itself. That's consistent with the current Ninth Thesis (Ellery included) suspecting a single source behind the incidents without knowing what it actually is.

relationship_to_secret_society.decision: CONFIRMED — The Ninth Thesis IS the existing Secret Society entity. Not a distinct-but-allied group; they're the same organization and the two data entities need to be smartly merged into one.

merge_plan_proposed.surviving_id: ninth_thesis (proposed) — it's already visibility:player and already tied to completed Session 2 canon, so the new PCs could plausibly have heard the name as campus legend. 'secret_society' would be retired/redirected into it.
merge_plan_proposed.mechanism: Use the schema's existing dm-only-content-block convention: the entity stays visibility:player with the public-facing 'campus legend' framing at the top of its content, and the true nature (it's a real active organization, Voss leads it, what they actually know/do) goes in a <div class="dm-only"> block inside the same file — rather than keeping a separate dm-only faction entity.
merge_plan_proposed.backlink_migration_needed: Full, grep-verified list now in founders_persona_audit.json → backlink_migration_list (supersedes the old partial list that used to live here).
merge_plan_proposed.status: Plan drafted, not yet executed against live data. Who-founded-it is decided on the reboot side (below), but founders_persona_audit.json (2026-07-27) found this contradicts brennan_ashcroft.html/secret_society.html's existing live claim that Ashcroft founded it as 'The Alumni Society' — that conflict needs a DM decision (see the audit doc's resolution options) before this merge can execute, not just a green light.

who_founded_it.decision: CONFIRMED — Option B. Aldric Voss (founder) quietly arranged for Wren Halloway's thesis to be pulled from the record and preserved rather than lost, and built the organization around it privately as a contingency alongside the Academy's official wards.
who_founded_it.age: Founded within the first several years of the Academy's ~350-year history (right after the first class graduated, while Voss was still active on campus) — roughly as old as the Academy itself, comfortably past the 200+ year minimum.
who_founded_it.leadership_lineage: The organization has been led by successive generations of the Voss family since Aldric founded it, with Dr. Ellery Voss the latest to run it. Exact line of succession between Aldric and Ellery (how many generations, any gaps or non-Voss interim leaders) is placeholder — not yet needed unless the plot calls for it.
who_founded_it.tone_guardrail: Write this as prudence, not manipulation — Voss didn't fabricate or alter anything, he preserved a true document that was about to be quietly discarded and let it speak for itself rather than issuing orders. Keeps this consistent with the founders-persona-rewrite decision (they were sincerely good; this is hedging, not conspiring).

relationship_to_phase1_voss_notes_clue.decision: CONFIRMED — the party finds Voss's notes, which are Ninth Thesis materials. Whether Voss left them findable by accident or on purpose is left ambiguous/intentional-leaning ('potentially at her intention') — this ties her to the organization and ties their investigation directly into the party's hook. Applied to phase1_something_is_happening.json.

continuity_flag: Feeds into the pending founders-persona audit noted in campaign_arc.json (secret_society's existing tags lean conspiratorial/sinister — needs reconciling with 'hunts hidden evil, currently allied with the party's goals' as part of the merge content pass).

operational_profile._purpose: Added 2026-07-24 to support Session 1's recruitment pitch (see session1_something_is_happening.json → structure.the_voss_summons) — Voss names the organization directly and makes a real recruitment offer, so the DM needs answers ready for follow-up questions, not just founding history.

scale_and_membership.size: Small and deliberately so — a loose network of roughly a dozen active operatives scattered across the region and beyond, not an institution. Voss selects people personally; there's no application process, no roster anyone outside the organization has ever seen.
scale_and_membership.composition: A mix of Academy alumni (the majority) and a handful of outside specialists Voss has recruited over the years for skills the alumni pool doesn't cover. No current students until now — the party would be the first active operatives still enrolled.
scale_and_membership.structure: Voss runs it personally; she is the only point of contact for any operative. No council, no hierarchy beneath her. Operatives generally don't know who else is in the organization unless Voss chooses to introduce them — compartmentalized more from institutional caution than secrecy theater.

sample_existing_operatives.sketch: A retired battle-cleric working the eastern borderlands, mostly investigating cult activity — the closest thing the organization has to a 'senior' field agent. Has been quietly asked to look into the Academy's incidents from the outside and found nothing actionable.

A pair of Academy graduates, some years out, who work the trade routes as caravan guards — cover for tracking rumors and contraband across several city-states. Good at long-haul information gathering, not built for close campus investigation.
One alumnus embedded in a distant city's magistrate's office — mostly useful for records and legal cover, not fieldwork.

why_the_party_specifically.the_real_reason: CONFIRMED — this is Voss's actual answer if pressed on 'why us': every existing operative is an outsider to campus life now, however capable. They can't walk the halls, sit in on lectures, or overhear faculty gossip without raising exactly the kind of attention that would tip off whoever's behind this. The party doesn't have that problem — they belong there, above suspicion, with better day-to-day access to the Academy than any Ninth Thesis field agent could get without years spent rebuilding a cover that these four already have for free. That's the actual pitch, not flattery.
why_the_party_specifically.guntrah_specifically: On top of the structural advantage above, Guntrah's Investigator background and demonstrated aptitude make him personally the piece she's been missing — someone who can actually turn access into answers. She says as much to him directly.

what_operatives_do.mandate: Investigate credible leads on 'hidden evil' — Voss's own phrase, deliberately broad. In practice: things that look wrong in a way institutions won't or can't act on. No formal jurisdiction; operatives go where the lead goes.
what_operatives_do.day_to_day: No chain of command beyond reporting findings back to Voss, generally in person or via a trusted courier method she'll explain if asked (a code phrase to a specific contact — details open, invent at the table if it comes up). Operatives are expected to use judgment, not wait for orders.
what_operatives_do.current_case: Right now: the pattern of planted-item incidents at the Academy this year, and whatever's behind it. That's the immediate ask. What it turns into after Session 1's discovery (Phase 2 onward) is intentionally open-ended from the party's perspective at this point — Voss doesn't oversell the scope up front.

resources_provided.funding: Modest but real — the organization isn't wealthy, but Voss can authorize reasonable expenses for a specific lead (travel, lodging, a bribe, replacement gear lost in the field). Not a blank check; she expects an accounting, not out of distrust but because that's how she runs everything.
resources_provided.information: Access to whatever the organization already knows that's relevant — which on THIS case is mostly what's in her notes (the party's already read those) plus whatever her other operatives' dead ends have ruled out.
resources_provided.cover: None needed on campus (that's the whole point) but she can vouch for them / open doors with contacts elsewhere once they're off-campus, on a case-by-case basis.
resources_provided.no_magic_bailout: No standing magical support, no cavalry — this is a small, quiet organization, not an institution with resources to spare. Consistent with 'they don't have the numbers to have already cracked this.'

secrecy_expectations.tone: Discretion requested, not demanded. Voss isn't running a cult of silence — she'd rather they not advertise it campus-wide (for the same reason outside operatives can't work openly: it tips off whoever's responsible), but there's no blood oath, no threat if they talk. Fits her established personality — direct, doesn't need theatrics to make a point land.
secrecy_expectations.campus_legend_status: Per relationship_to_secret_society above, 'the Secret Society' already exists as vague campus legend/rumor the new party may have heard of before this scene (harmless-sounding, half-joke, the way any school has an urban legend). Voss confirming it's real is the actual reveal here, not the concept of secrecy itself.

operational_profile.if_they_decline: No pressure, no consequence. She made the offer once, sincerely, and will respect a no without repeating the pitch or holding it against them. Consistent with her character — she doesn't coerce, she selects. Leaves the door open implicitly ('the offer doesn't expire') without saying so outright.
